column1: The effects of the coronavirus will weigh on economic activity in the near term and pose risks to the economic outlook, and the FOMC’s rapid move to the effective lower bound with large-scale Treasury and MBS purchases, expanded repos, and enhanced discount window access aligns with the literature on acting forcefully in demand collapses amplified by financial frictions. Research on the credit channel (e.g., Bernanke–Gertler; Gertler and Gilchrist; Oliner and Rudebusch) emphasizes how deteriorating balance sheets and tighter credit conditions magnify downturns, supporting the Fed’s emphasis on keeping funding markets liquid and credit flowing. With market-based inflation compensation falling and surveys little changed, inflation expectations management via forward-looking frameworks (Svensson’s inflation-forecast targeting) and adherence to a symmetric 2% objective are consistent with minimizing losses in a standard quadratic central-bank loss function while at the zero lower bound. The open-economy toolkit, including dollar liquidity swap lines, is also consistent with new open economy macro insights (Lane; Engel; Corsetti–Presenti) that global financial conditions can transmit and amplify shocks. Netting these points, the near-term outlook remains negatively skewed, but decisive policy reduces tail risks of a deeper credit-driven contraction. sentiment score = -0.40
